# sealift

> Prepares npm dependency updates for air-gapped networks. On the connected side, it analyses a project's package.json with pnpm and Trivy, ranks the newer versions of each direct dependency by known CVEs, proposes the oldest version that fixes the most, and packs the chosen versions into packages_npm.tar.gz for a Nexus import on the air-gapped side. One Go binary with a React interface, shipped as the image ghcr.io/morgankryze/sealift for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. GPL-3.0.

Limits: Python (pip) projects are collected through the API only, with no collection screen; the import screens take them. Input is a package.json whose direct dependencies are pinned to exact versions; no lockfile, workspaces, overrides or resolutions. Only direct dependencies get new versions; transitive ones change through them, without the minimum release age. The archive holds only the changed dependencies' trees. A session keeps the target platform it started with. Each export carries manifest.json.sig, an Ed25519 signature of manifest.json made with a key sealift generates for its volume; the import trusts one public key carried once to its settings (publicKeyFile). The signature does not show who asked for an export or how old it is, and the reports are not signed. A regenerated key or a lost volume means carrying a new public key. sealift has no login. A malicious package with no published CVE is not detected.

Deployment: at start, sealift downloads Trivy 0.76.2, pinned by version and sha256 in its binary, the vulnerability database, and the default targets' pnpm and uv, with no click. /healthz answers 503 with the missing items until all are ready, then 200; /livez answers 200 while the server runs. A policy file named by SEALIFT_POLICY sets the targets, the limits and the brand; no screen or API route changes them, and none installs a tool.

Defaults: minimum release age 14 days (range 1 to 90), resolve parallelism 4 (1 to 16), download parallelism 16 (1 to 32), npm target Linux x64 glibc with Node 22.17.1 and pnpm 10.34.5, pip target Linux x86_64 glibc 2.28 with Python 3.11.2 and uv 0.13.7.

## Docs

- [Overview](docs/overview.md): the two roles, context and crossing diagrams, the collection and import pipelines, what each check proves, the /data layout, a glossary
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): docker run, the preparation at start, a first archive from a five-dependency project
- [Workflow](docs/workflow.md): each screen of a session with every button label
- [How sealift chooses](docs/how-sealift-chooses.md): CVE vectors by severity, tie-breaks, the eight signals, the minimum release age, the review groups
- [Settings](docs/settings.md): the policy file with every key, default and range, the brand, settings saved by 0.7.0, the read-only panel, the signing key
- [The air gap](docs/air-gap.md): the archive, the signature and the trusted key, the reports, sha256 checks, the import, lockfile drift
- [Importing](docs/importing.md): the import service screens: Archives, Imports and one import, the trusted key, every state and the retry card
- [Python projects](docs/python.md): a pip project through the API: requirements files, the target, analysis, export, import and the install from Nexus
- [Deployment](docs/deployment.md): hardened Compose, capabilities, readiness with /healthz and /livez, the policy overlay, reverse proxy with SSE, outbound hosts, the /data volume, the key the import trusts, upgrades from 0.7.0 and the rollback, backups
- [Runbook](docs/runbook.md): both sides from nothing to a first import: the drop-in values, Harbor, the Secret, the ingress and oauth2-proxy values, a checklist, upgrades, backups, the worst cases on a shared Nexus repository and the rollback list
- [Helm chart](docs/helm.md): the chart of the import service, every value, the `token.header` setting, the install notes, Argo CD and the release
- [Request to the administrators](docs/admin-request.md): the MinIO, Nexus and Keycloak accounts and the infrastructure the install needs, with the reason for each
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): each message with its cause and fix
- [FAQ](docs/faq.md): lockfiles, transitive dependencies, other ecosystems, data, reset

- [Web](docs/dev/web.md): routes, step bar, job events, checking a screen in a browser
- [api/openapi.yaml](api/openapi.yaml): the API contract
